content.title: About
content.content: Cooked cucumber is a cucumber that has been peeled and boiled in lightly salted water until tender. Most vitamins and minerals are retained during the heat treatment, while the texture becomes softer, making it suitable for baby foods and diet dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cucumbers belong to the gourd family and are close relatives of zucchini and pumpkin.
Cooked cucumber is a common ingredient in Eastern European dishes such as rassolnik or as a filling for pies.
Heat reduces the natural bitterness, giving the cucumber a milder flavor.
Cucumbers consist of more than 95 % water, providing hydration even after cooking.
In some cultures, cooked cucumber is served with vinegar and spices as a side dish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Cooked cucumber retains a good amount of vitamin K, which is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Although some vitamin C is lost during cooking, cucumber still provides a notable amount of this antioxidant.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One cup of cooked cucumber contains fewer than 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports proper heart function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in cucumber promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cucumbers, manifested as itching, swelling, or rash.

items.title: Loss of heat‑sensitive nutrients
items.content: Cooking reduces the content of vitamin C and certain heat‑sensitive antioxidants.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If boiled in salted water, the sodium level can become high; it is advisable to use moderate amounts of salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked cucumber can be served as a standalone snack, added to salads, soups, stews, or used in baby purees. Cut it into cubes or slices and season with dill, garlic, lemon juice, or a light yogurt dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cucumber in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portioned pieces after patting them dry to remove excess moisture.

luncheon-slice-meatless-beef-chicken-sal.title: Luncheon slice, meatless-beef, chicken, salami or turkey

content.title: About
content.content: Luncheon slice is a ready‑to‑eat meat deli product offered in meatless‑beef, chicken, salami and turkey versions. It is made from selected meat cuts, seasoned with a blend of spices and vacuum‑packed to preserve freshness. The slice is convenient for quick snacks, sandwiches or salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Luncheon slice is a staple in office cafeterias because it stays safe to eat without cooking for several days.
The meatless‑beef version was created for consumers avoiding red meat while still wanting the classic deli flavor.
Salami in this product follows traditional Italian curing methods with paprika and garlic.
Turkey provides a leaner alternative, making that variant lower in calories.
Each package is sealed in an airtight film, allowing refrigeration for up to 14 days.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A typical serving delivers about 12 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat variants provide dietary iron needed for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The product has virtually no sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific meat types.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt is used for preservation, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain variants may contain food preservatives that are not suitable for all consumers.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: Although ready to eat, the slice can be warmed to enhance flavor if desired.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Luncheon slice can be eaten straight from the pack, added to sandwiches, salads, wraps, or used in hot dishes such as omelets and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Discard if the product develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

nutritional-powder-mix-sugar-free-carnat.title: Nutritional powder mix, sugar free (Carnation Instant Breakfast)

content.title: About
content.content: The sugar‑free Nutritional powder mix Carnation Instant Breakfast is a dry breakfast beverage enriched with vitamins and minerals. It dissolves quickly in milk or water, providing a balanced blend of protein, carbohydrates and healthy fats without added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Designed for quick preparation and convenient for travel or work.
Provides 20% of the daily value of vitamin D and 30% of vitamin B12.
Contains no added sugar yet retains a pleasant creamy taste thanks to natural sweeteners.
Suitable for vegetarians but not vegans because of dairy ingredients.
Package yields 30 servings; each serving is 30 g.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6, B12 and niacin support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Help maintain healthy bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Each serving delivers about 8 g of protein, aiding muscle repair.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Suitable for individuals monitoring blood glucose levels.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Supports normal blood formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains milk powder and may cause discomfort for those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein should avoid consumption.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Those limiting salt intake should monitor total daily sodium.

items.title: Not a complete meal replacement
items.content: The powder is intended as a supplement, not as the sole source of nutrition.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix one serving (30 g) of powder with 200‑250 ml of milk, water or a plant‑based beverage, stirring until fully dissolved. Add fruit, nuts or honey for extra flavor if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. After opening, use within 3‑4 weeks for best quality.

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen cheese pizza with thin crust is a convenient ready‑to‑cook product that bakes quickly in the oven. The crisp thin dough is topped with tomato sauce and a generous layer of melted cheese. It is intended for home use and should be stored at –18 °C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust requires a higher baking temperature than traditional thick crust.
The cheese blend usually combines mozzarella and cheddar for optimal melt and flavor.
Frozen pizzas often undergo double‑freeze processing to preserve dough texture and sauce aroma.
Cheese pizza is one of the most popular frozen pizza flavors worldwide.
Thin crust reduces the overall calorie count compared with a thick‑crust pizza.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese provides a good amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Cheese contributes significant protein, supporting tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese contain vitamins B2 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible carbs
items.content: Thin crust contains less starch than a fluffy crust, making it easier on digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made pizzas often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some cheese blends and dough formulations may contain trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: To extend shelf life, preservatives may be added, which some consumers prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200–220 °C, place the pizza on a rack or baking sheet, and bake for 10–12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly. Slice into portions and serve with a green salad or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen pizza at –18 °C or lower in its sealed packaging. Once thawed, consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

rice-white-with-cheese-and-or-cream-base.title: White Rice with Cheese and/or Cream Sauce, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: White rice prepared with a cheese or cream‑based sauce and added fat is a calorie‑dense side dish with a soft texture and a rich, buttery flavor. The fat increases the energy value and enhances the perception of taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream sauces are often made from butter, cream, and cheese, giving the dish a luxurious mouthfeel.
In cooking, white rice is used as a neutral base that lets sauces shine.
Adding fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and D present in the sauce.
These dishes are traditional in both Asian and Mediterranean cuisines.
When cooked with the correct water‑to‑rice ratio, the grains stay separate and do not become mushy.

items.title: High Energy Content
items.content: The fat and cheese sauce raise the calorie count, which can be beneficial for individuals with increased energy needs.

items.title: Source of Calcium
items.content: Cheese sauce provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice supplies B1, B3 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Fat‑Soluble Vitamins
items.content: The added fat aids the absorption of vitamins A, D, E and K if they are present in the sauce.

items.title: Enhanced Flavor Perception
items.content: Fat amplifies aroma and prolongs the taste experience.

items.title: High Calorie Density
items.content: The dish is calorie‑rich and may contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated Fat Content
items.content: Cream sauces contain saturated fats, which in excess can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: Cheese and cream may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Sodium Levels
items.content: Cheese sauces are often salty, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, drizzled with the cheese or cream sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs, chopped parsley, or sautéed vegetables for variety. The dish pairs well with meat, fish, or vegetable patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Store the sauce separately and reheat together with the rice if needed. Frozen portions can be stored for up to 2 months.
